runs.text: What is an advantage of international specialisation?

cells.text: countries become overdependent on each other

runs.text: Skin creams preventing sunburn made in the European Union (EU) are more effective than those made in the United States (US). US tourists stock up on the creams when visiting Europe. Such creams are banned from production in the US because of the chemicals in them. In 2013, negotiations began to remove this ban in order to allow production in the US.
How is this freer trade likely to affect manufacturers of skin creams in the US and the EU?
What is most likely to encourage international specialisation?

cells.text: similarities in climate in different countries
the ability to produce products more cheaply than other countries

What is a disadvantage of this?

cells.text: Countries have a constant demand for raw materials.
International trade only benefits the importing countries.
It is necessary for low-income countries to belong to a free trade area.

runs.text: What is a disadvantage of increased specialisation by a country?

cells.text: It becomes more reliant on imports to meet all its needs.
It reduces the potential for international trade.
It results in access to a greater variety of goods for consumers.
It results in lower costs for home produced goods.

What is a disadvantage of increasing international specialisation?

cells.text: Consumers pay higher prices for goods and services reducing their welfare.
Domestic firms may be uncompetitive leading to structural unemployment.
Domestic firms may experience rising costs as they pay more for imports.
Resources may be used less efficiently as domestic firms face less competition.

runs.text: Which result of increased specialisation in a firm is an advantage for the firm, but a disadvantage for some of the workers in the firm?
A country specialises in the production of steel, toys and textiles.
What is a disadvantage of specialisation for the country’s workers?

cells.text: They cannot afford to buy products from other countries.
They could become structurally unemployed if global demand changes.
They have to learn a variety of skills.
They have too much choice which wastes their time.

runs.text: Malaysia and Indonesia specialise in the production of palm oil.
What is a disadvantage of specialisation?

cells.text: concentration of labour in the activity in which it is most productive

reliance on trade with other countries for other goods
